failure.cause: Julia JSON encoded a Float64 radius multiplier equal to 1.0 as the JSON number 1; Python json decoded that token as int 1, so str(radius_multiplier) produced '1' while the frozen analyzer looked up '1.0'.
failure.boundary: The frozen analyzer completed result/source/runtime/checkpoint/raw replay checks before entering independent numerical reconstruction. It crashed on representation lookup before writing independent-analysis.json.

repair.normalization: On an in-memory deep copy passed only to frozen analyze, replace radius_multiplier with float 1.0 exactly when type(radius_multiplier) is int and value equals 1.
repair.unchanged_values: Existing floats, 0.5, booleans, strings, nulls and all other values are passed unchanged to the frozen analyzer; the wrapper introduces no new numeric-radius acceptance gate.
repair.frozen_analyzer_execution: Read the approved original analyzer bytes once, hash those bytes, compile and execute those same bytes, then replace only the global analyze call with the deep-copy adapter.
repair.canonical_cli: Accept exactly four argument tokens in fixed order: one full --result-directory/value pair followed by one full --experiment-directory/value pair; require the experiment path to equal the wrapper directory.
repair.terminal_provenance: Before analysis and immediately before the A9 terminal binding, verify exact result/checkpoint sets, all 36 checkpoint payload hashes, result bindings and artifacts, the implementation freeze and all 37 implementation sources, plus direct input-freeze/input-manifest/Gold bindings.
repair.analysis_output: Hash and parse one independent-analysis byte snapshot, reverify it unchanged, then atomically publish a separate A9 binding file.
